key_insight: A founder-population GWAS/exome analysis of ICU patients identified a likely loss-of-function UBE2L3 variant that may influence sepsis susceptibility.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests UBE2L3 could become a biomarker or therapeutic target for understanding and potentially stratifying sepsis risk, but it is not yet ready for clinical use.
method: WGS-based GWAS and exome-wide analysis in 210 Arab ICU patients
Prioritized deleterious founder variants using REGENIE Firth regression, CADD, and population enrichment filters
Validated signal with external All of Us burden testing and mouse functional context
evidence_signal: The strongest case-level signal was a novel UBE2L3 start-loss variant found in 3 of 68 sepsis cases and 0 of 142 controls (Fisher's exact P = 0.026), with supportive external burden evidence in All of Us for bacterial infection.
watch_item: The association signals are based on small case counts and wide confidence intervals, so replication in larger diverse cohorts is needed before implementation.
paper_title: Genome-Wide Association Study of Sepsis Susceptibility in ICU Patients Identifies Arab Founder Loss-of-Function Variant in UBE2L3
